reason: Repeatable workflow from this window: a single static nginx container serving nine satellite domains by Host header, per-domain vhosts generated from a template, article-style pages with a long-keyword target for the main site. The window shows the ordering that matters (origin proof, then DNS, then certs). No existing skill covers static satellite/backlink sites.
Trigger cue too narrow; the episode built nine satellite blog domains and the index line missed "satellite blog" wording a user would type.
Article length floor and pre-upload copy scan were applied ad hoc in this episode; they belong in the microsite build step so the next network build does not rediscover them.
Per-page verification in this episode (200, one h1, main-site link count) worked and should be the standing check, with the footer-repeat failure made explicit.

User asked whether any other domain could link to the main site; the answer first said only one domain could, which was wrong. Rule: enumerate every microsite before answering no, and solve topic fit with an article angle.

Server-side deploy of microsite HTML had no restore point, and post-deploy checks skipped the sitemap. Add a tar backup in the same ssh command as the extract, and a count check of sitemap entries against the article count.
